title: Ayah Lens demo script Version 3
status: Version 3 approved; English switch implemented and wearer-verified in Build 31; footage capture starting
opening_note: Let viewers experience unfamiliar recitation, then reveal its meaning through genuine output. Explain the population and Meta implementation after that experience. Keep the uninterrupted proof section intact.
production_notes: The first 16 seconds are an edited before-and-after reveal. The separate 1:00–1:30 proof section is a genuine uninterrupted recording.

The proposed opening reference is 94:5. Its exact Pickthall English is “But lo! with hardship goeth ease,”. Capture a real successful run before using it. Use a proven passage if this opener is unreliable.
The viewer condition matters: say “If Arabic is unfamiliar.” Do not assume that every judge is unfamiliar with Arabic or claim that all Muslims lack understanding.
The prayer scene presents a possible use. Keep its religious-permissibility disclaimer readable beside the scene and repeat it in the final video description.

The Show English meaning switch is implemented in Build 31. The wearer confirmed English disappears and returns on phone and glasses while Arabic keeps following. Capture the actual control in a separate take.

If the translation switch is unavailable, replace the 2:18–2:32 narration with: “The phone preview mirrors the selected lens window. The full passage remains available on the phone. The glasses keep a compact portion in view as the recitation continues.”
The source text is published Tanzil Arabic and Pickthall English. Spark supplies paired source boundaries; it does not author the displayed translation.
The filmed long-passage plans are cached. Voice transcription is live. Complete reference coverage is not a full-Quran accuracy result.
The population estimate comes from Pew Research Center: https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/06/10/islam-was-the-worlds-fastest-growing-religion-from-2010-to-2020/
Create text, diagrams and labels in post. Do not generate scripture text inside imagery. Preserve the original published wording.
Any enlarged phone preview or explanatory graphic remains labelled. Show the actual compact glasses display accurately.

Optional stretch reveal: a second person selects a prepared recitation excerpt while hands stay off the phone. Film only after successful acquisition/recovery checks. Do not call this any-verse or blind full-Quran accuracy proof.
Present Hifz as using an Arabic reference while rehearsing. Demonstrate the existing visibility switch and recitation-following behavior.

Quran teaching is a future direction requiring dedicated development and extensive evaluation with qualified teachers. The current implementation uses pretrained Muse models; no specialized teaching model has been trained or validated.
rubric_notes: Impact 30%: turn an unfamiliar-language listening experience into something the viewer can personally recognize, then establish population scale and prayer/home use.
Meta tooling 25%: connect the glasses, live speech model and Spark-assisted source pairing to the visible experience. Explain cached plans honestly.
Technical execution 20%: make within-passage movement the second reveal, followed by source preservation, actual implementation evidence and tests.
Demo 25%: use the edited opening reveal, a genuine 30-second continuous take, matched scenes and a closing return to the original image.

segments.title: Make the experience universal
segments.narration: If Arabic is unfamiliar, you just felt the gap between hearing words and following their meaning. About two billion people are Muslim. For many of us, that gap is part of everyday listening. What if the meaning could stay with us?
segments.visual: Return to the same listener. Let the population figure appear briefly beside real human footage. The number gives scale after the viewer has experienced the need. Keep the small population source caption readable.

segments.narration: Meet Ayah Lens. Meta glasses, Muse Voice, and Muse Spark, working together to bring Quran recitation and its English meaning into view.

segments.title: Carry one listening experience between settings
segments.narration: During Salat, Muslim prayer, it could help listeners follow the recitation. At home, it can follow a reciter playing on television. Hands free.
segments.visual: Match the wearer’s position across a proposed prayer scene and the television listening scene. Let the same frame composition connect the settings. Keep the religious-permissibility disclaimer visible for the entire prayer scene. Use cleared recitation footage and audio.

segments.title: Reveal the difficult part hiding in plain sight
segments.narration: Now look closer. We are still inside the same passage. A long verse cannot fit on this lens. Ayah Lens follows the recitation through it, showing the relevant portion as the words continue. Nobody is turning a page.

segments.title: Explain the actual AI and tracking work
segments.narration: Muse Voice converts the glasses’ audio into Arabic text. Muse Spark helps pair Arabic phrases with portions of a published English translation. It can also assist with uncertain passage matches. Our software tracks the position, validates the source boundaries, and sends the current portion to the glasses.

segments.title: Establish the working foundation
segments.narration: The reference covers all 114 surahs. We built the glasses integration and automatic following during this hackathon. Fifty-five tests cover matching, source preservation, and display scheduling. With further development and extensive testing, future versions could support Quran teaching.
segments.visual: Keep the working product prominent. Show brief readable inserts of the actual source library, event-dated Git history and verified test result. Then introduce a short card labelled Future: teaching support, requires extensive testing. Complete reference coverage remains separate from recognition accuracy; the teaching card describes future work.
